method_card.title: Averages and Spread
steps: Mean: add all values, divide by how many (\(\sum fx \div \sum f\) for a table).
Median: middle of the ordered data. Mode: most common value.
Grouped data: use class midpoints for the mean; highest frequency gives the modal class.
Range = largest − smallest. IQR = Q3 − Q1, less swayed by outliers.
method_card.content:
Averages summarise data with one number; spread says how varied it is.

The mean shares the total equally: \(\frac{\sum fx}{\sum f}\) for a frequency table. For grouped data, use each class midpoint. The median is the middle of the ordered values; the mode is the most common.

Range = largest − smallest. The interquartile range, Q3 − Q1, ignores the extremes, so it is steadier when there are outliers.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Find one average (mean, median or mode) or the range from a short list of numbers.
problem_bank.silver_description: Averages and spread from frequency tables and grouped data, including quartiles, the IQR and combined means.
problem_bank.gold_description: Work backwards from an average to a missing value, and estimate means from grouped or combined data.

bronze.title: Bronze: one average from a list
steps: Mean: add every value, then divide by how many there are.
Median: put the values in order and take the middle one. With an even count, average the middle two.
Mode is the most common value. Range is largest minus smallest, a measure of spread.

steps.label: Check
steps.content: Five values, so the middle is the 3rd.

silver.title: Silver: tables, groups and spread
steps: Frequency table mean: multiply each value by its frequency, add to get \(\sum fx\), then divide by the total frequency \(\sum f\).
Grouped data: use the midpoint of each class as its value, then take the same \(\sum fx \div \sum f\).
IQR is Q3 minus Q1. The modal class has the highest frequency; the median class holds the middle position.

gold.title: Gold: work backwards and estimate
steps: Missing value: turn the mean into a total (mean × how many), then use what you know to find the gap.
Combined mean: add the group totals, add the group sizes, then divide. Never just average the two means.
Grouped estimate: midpoints give \(\sum fx\), then divide by \(\sum f\); round if it does not come out exactly.
